the realism of synthetic images can be improved by translating the images to the empirical domain, and that the realism is improved by increasing the similarity of the color, texture, and morphology distributions of the synthetic and empirical data.
synthetic agricultural images can be optimised to increase the realism of the images by translating them from synthetic to empirical domain.
synthetic images can be translated into empirical images, but not vice versa.

the development of a novel method to improve the realism of synthetic images for agricultural robotics.

the translation of synthetic images to empirical images, enabling the use of synthetic data in the development of deep learning algorithms for image segmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cycle GANs are a powerful and effective method to translate synthetic agricultural images into a more realistic domain, but that this is dependent on the type of data, e.g. local versus global features.
the synthetic images can be translated to the empirical images, but that the realism of the global features is still not fully captured.
synthetic images can be optimised to be more realistic for a given dataset, which is a first step towards the creation of large annotated datasets for training deep neural networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synthetic images can be optimised using Cycle GANs for the use case of machine learning for agricultural image segmentation.
the proposed approach is a promising method to close the realism gap in synthetic datasets for agricultural robotics, which can be applied in other agricultural domains as well.

the realism of synthetic images can be optimised for the Capsicum annuem (sweet or bell) pepper dataset using cycle GANs, which enables the generation of a synthetic dataset that can be used for machine learning tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synthetic datasets can be used as an alternative to large empirical datasets for plant part image classification and segmentation.
synthetic data can be optimised to increase the realism of the data, which can be used to increase the accuracy and robustness of machine learning algorithms.

cycle generative adversial networks can be successfully applied to increase the realism of synthetic images, closing the gap between the empirical and synthetic domain, and thus enabling machine learning on large synthetic datasets.
